bearings.paper_claim: Intensity is each speech's mean F0 z-scored against the speaker's own baseline, in SD units. Table 1 pitch models (N1 = 74,151 speeches, N2 = 619 members, 2009-2014 House floor): female x 'women' mentioned = 0.090 (SE 0.027) without controls and 0.112 (SE 0.027) with controls. About 120 speeches per member is only the average (74,151 / 619); the paper states no required sample size. The authors call the raw magnitude 'slight enough'.
bearings.system_side: Candidate descriptor converts eGeMAPS semitones to Hz (code comment cites Dietrich, Hayes and O'Brien at line 210), z-scores each speech unit against the member mean and SD inside _speaker_pitch_profile, and reports topic_emotional_intensity as mean deviation per transcript topic. Floors: 5 speech units per member, 2 distinct topics, 2 units per reported topic. No comparison group. Default status CANDIDATE_CONSUMED_BY_NOTHING_AWAITING_USER_RATIFICATION (line 273). The brain's count of 0 accepted v2 clips was not checked.
bearings.code_ref: fec/members/b5_audio_descriptors_candidate.py:209-254 (comment line 210; standardization and topic summary); fec/audio_rules.py:20-22 (floors 5 / 2 / 2)
bearings.transfer_conditions: The within-speaker z transform transfers. The inference does not: the paper identifies effects from a cross-speaker contrast over 74,151 speeches, while the system computes one member's topic mean from 2-5 units. Assuming independent units, the SE of a 2-5 unit topic mean is about 0.45-0.7 SD (arithmetic; no minimum detectable effect was computed). The paper's effects are 0.09-0.38 SD.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 1 numbers, the standardization and the floors are confirmed in code and text. Softened: the paper does not say a member needs about 120 speeches; that figure is an average. The power statement is arithmetic under an independence assumption, not a computed detection threshold.

bearings.paper_claim: Pitch measures arousal, not valence (footnote 1, p. 942). The paper adds controls for speech duration, a one-minute dummy and an election-year dummy (p. 946, Table 1). It acknowledges that question intonation also moves mean F0 (footnote 8, p. 945) but does not control for it, arguing mean pitch remains reliable. The baseline is one venue: the House floor via HouseLive.
bearings.paper_location: fn 1 p. 942; fn 8 p. 945; p. 946 controls; Table 1
bearings.system_side: The baseline pools all accepted units for a member across at least 2 programs. Channel (studio, remote, telephone) is recorded in the brain as uncontrolled. Neither the per-member z nor the Washington Journal subject_effects centering has a duration, question or speech-type term. The WJ table on the desk shows topic shifts from as few as 2 reactions. The brain channel note was not checked.
bearings.code_ref: fec/members/b5_audio_descriptors_candidate.py (baseline and z, roughly lines 229-249); fec/speech/build_descriptive_speech.py:2491-2531 (member centering) and :2521 (minimum 2 reactions); fec/surfaces/templates/make_member_desk_00.tpl:1280 (WJ reactions display)
bearings.transfer_conditions: Applies wherever the system compares a member's pitch across topics. The paper's controls cover duration and one-minute speeches but not question intonation, so the system's gap is wider than the analyst stated. Program or channel offsets can exceed the paper's 0.1 SD effects, so a topic concentrated on one program picks up that offset. 'Relative emotional intensity' must not be read as anger or enthusiasm.
bearings.verifier_note: Softened: the paper does not add question intonation as a control; it names it as a confound it does not model. Duration and one-minute controls are real. Code gaps confirmed: no duration, question or speech-type term in either centering, and the 2-reaction minimum is in place. The channel note is brain-sourced and not checked.

bearings.paper_claim: Raw F0 differs mainly by sex: Table 2 gives female means of about 203-206 Hz and male means of about 151 Hz. Deviation from each speaker's own baseline removes stable between-speaker level by construction. The authors read the measure as an emotional disposition toward an issue, and say the slight changes are consistent with pitch indicating a lawmaker's emotional disposition toward an issue.
bearings.paper_location: p. 945-946; Table 2 p. 948; issue-commitment discussion (page not confirmed in extracted text)
bearings.system_side: Output contract sets absolute_f0_enters_personality to False and audio_may_modify_big_five to False, and excludes absolute F0 or inferred gender as a personality input. The brain's sex-confound correlation (r = -0.266) and the audio-N MISS at N = 90 are brain-sourced and were not checked.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Excluding absolute F0 from personality scores is directly supported by Table 2. The paper gives no evidence that pitch measures a between-member disposition such as N, so the closed audio-N route is consistent with it. The paper's own gloss is a topic-specific emotional disposition, which the rel calls a state; it is an interpretation the authors do not test.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 2 values and the exclusion lines are confirmed. Softened: the paper frames the measure as a disposition toward issues and leaves room for a trait-like reading, so 'a topic-level state, not a trait' overstates what the paper establishes. The brain figures were not checked.

bearings.paper_claim: The corpus is Clerk HouseLive video, audio and closed captions: 6,432 hours from 863 House debates, 6 Jan 2009 to 4 Aug 2014. Speeches are split on caption timestamps, giving 74,158 speeches of at least 50 words. The captioning vendor asserts about 95 percent word accuracy (footnote 11). The authors transcribed 100 random speeches and found the captions 'essentially mirrored' them. The paper does not say the chamber attributes each speech to a member.
bearings.system_side: Clips are kept when Haiku 4.5 reads YouTube auto-captions and returns SOLO_TARGET with identity MATCH or NEUTRAL. The brain's share of kept clips with no identifying content (33.7 percent) and the pre-2026-07-09 contamination figure (38 percent) are brain-sourced and were not checked.
bearings.code_ref: fec/members/b5_audio_verify.py:7 (docstring) and :77 (Haiku 4.5 call; keep rule follows it)
bearings.transfer_conditions: Clerk speaker attribution is not established by the paper, so using it as an identity source needs a separate check of Clerk floor video metadata. If confirmed, House floor video from 2009 onward could replace guessed identity on floor clips. It does not reach interview, Sunday-show, Senate or hearing audio, where the identity gap is largest.
bearings.verifier_note: Corpus size, dates, the 95 percent vendor figure and the keep rule are confirmed. Softened: 'the chamber has already identified the speaker' is not in the paper, and 'matched' overstates 'essentially mirrored'. The brain percentages were not checked.

bearings.paper_claim: Speech topic, word choice and length of remarks are highly controllable and driven by strategic concerns, while vocal pitch typically lies beyond the individual's control, making it a more honest indicator of intensity on a given issue (leakage hierarchy, pp. 942-944). The paper does not compare dictionary tone or LSD scores with pitch.
bearings.system_side: Press intensity is |LSD net| / words or (pos + neg) / words (lsd_charge) per member press release. The press pillar multiplies stance sign by this heat.
bearings.transfer_conditions: A theoretical argument only; the paper never tests LSD tone against pitch. The claim that press releases are staff-drafted and so more strategic than floor speech has no support in the paper or the code. LSD charge measures crafted rhetorical tone, not felt intensity, and should be labelled that way.
bearings.verifier_note: The leakage passage and code lines are confirmed. Softened: the paper says pitch is less controllable, not that audio gives an intensity signal that text cannot give. The staff-drafting claim is unsupported here.

bearings.paper_claim: Table 7, Model 7.1 gives 0.015 (SE 0.002) and Model 7.2 gives 0.012 (SE 0.002) for female speeches x female pitch on the share of male votes cast with female members. At +2 SD pitch (1.41 on the paper's scale), that share moves from 0.23 SD below to 0.53 SD above as female speeches go from 0 to 43 (Figure 3, p. 957). The authors say the data are observational and do not claim causation (p. 956-957). Vote timing is unknown (fn 31).
bearings.system_side: The cross-party cue weight is sqrt(bpf_u * bpf_v) (line 64). Searches of lt_priming.py found no intensity or pitch term in the cue weight or the pressure terms.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Weak and gender-specific: women's issues, 2009-2014, floor votes with no timestamps, not cosponsorship. The paper does not test a threshold mechanism, so it cannot set any engine constant.
bearings.verifier_note: Coefficients, the -0.23 to +0.53 SD range and the +2 SD condition match the paper. The code claim is confirmed: no intensity term. 'Absent or negative at low volume' is the rel's gloss; the paper gives a negative value at 0 speeches.

summary_issues: Sample and denominator: summary gives 74,158 speeches; Table 1 models use N1 = 74,151 speeches and 619 members. Both figures should name their window (2009-2014, House floor) and denominator.
'Hard-to-fake' is not the paper's term. The paper says pitch is difficult for speakers to control (abstract; p. 942).
'About 120 speeches per speaker' is an average (74,151 / 619), not a design parameter or a stated requirement.
'Male members mention women more' holds only in Table 5 Model 5.2 (interaction 0.011, p < 0.05); Model 5.1 is 0.009 and not significant.
'Raise their own pitch on the topic' rests on the three-way term in Table 6 (0.016, p < 0.01). The 'women mentioned' main effect is 0.026 and not significant.
'Male members do not change': the paper reports a 0.02 SD change that is essentially unchanged (t = 0.02, p about 0.99). State it as 0.02 SD, not significant.

'Partisans speak 0.29 to 0.38 SD higher on topics their party owns' comes from interaction terms in Table 4, ranging 0.288 to 0.380 across four models, in standardized units. Name them as interactions.
The paper's causal disclaimer is attributed to p. 957; the extracted text does not confirm that page (it appears around pp. 956-957).
'The chamber has already identified the speaker' in Clerk video is not stated in the paper and should be removed or marked as an open check.
The claim that the floors cannot detect 0.1-0.4 SD effects is arithmetic under an independence assumption (SE about 0.45-0.7 SD for 2-5 units). No minimum detectable effect was computed; say so.
Baseline pooling across interview programs is confirmed in code. Pooling across channels is not confirmed, and the brain's channel-uncontrolled note was not checked.

Brain-sourced claims (permutation null and commit 4193f0140, r = -0.266, audio-N MISS at N = 90, 33.7 and 38 percent clip shares, 0 accepted v2 clips) were not checked here. The live candidate file was confirmed to lack any null or sign_informative field. Under DE-062 they stay UNVERIFIED.
